findings.issue_text: **2. Stored XSS — `raw_html` posts are never sanitized.** (`app/models/post.rb:131`, `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`, `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13`, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19`)

`poll_feed` does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content...)` with **no tag/attribute whitelist**. The unescape actively converts a feed's escaped `<script>` into a live `<script>`. The result is stored as `cooked` and emitted via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed view *and* returned as `cooked` in topic JSON, where Ember inserts it as-is on the main forum. Feeds routinely carry third-party/user-contributed HTML.

`TopicEmbed.import` line 13 interpolates the URL into an attribute without escaping: `"#{url}"`. In the feed path `url` comes straight from `i.link`/`i.id`, and the only guard is a `^https?://` prefix match — so `http://x/'+onmouseover='alert(1)` passes validation and breaks out of the attribute. `I18n.t` does not escape interpolations.
`import_remote`'s Readability whitelist keeps `href` with **any value**, so `<a href="javascript:...">` survives.
**3. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — `i.content.scrub` crashes on RSS 2.0 feeds, killing the whole poll.**

**4. `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-15` — unauthenticated, unvalidated, unthrottled job enqueue.** `embed_url` is taken straight from the query string with no format or host validation and handed to `Jobs.enqueue`. Validation only happens *inside* the job, so anyone can enqueue unbounded Sidekiq work by varying the URL (the Redis throttle also runs inside the job and is keyed per-URL, so it doesn't help). Fix: validate scheme + host against `embeddable_host` in the controller before enqueueing, and apply a per-IP `RateLimiter`.

**5. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:15` / migration — no URL normalization.** Lookup and the unique index are exact string matches, so `?utm_source=…`, trailing slash, `http` vs `https`, and `#fragment` variants each create a *separate topic for the same article* — squarely against the stated "URL handling" intent. Also, `t.string :embed_url` is `varchar(255)` by default; a longer URL raises `StatementInvalid` inside the job. Fix: normalize (strip fragment, canonicalize scheme/host case, optionally strip tracking params) before lookup/insert and widen the column.

**6. `lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28` — non-atomic throttle can wedge a URL forever.** `SETNX` then a separate `EXPIRE`: if the process dies or Redis fails between the two calls, the key has no TTL and that URL is throttled permanently. Fix: `$redis.set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)`.
**7. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:62-70` — `absolutize_urls` handles only root-relative URLs.**
Protocol-relative `//cdn.example.com/x.png` starts with `/`, so `sub(/^\/+/,'')` mangles it into `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png` — a working URL is turned into a broken one.
Document-relative URLs (`images/x.png`, `../x.png`) are not rewritten at all and stay broken.
`<base href>` in the source document is ignored.
`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` uses `force: true`, which silently `DROP`s an existing `topic_embeds` table. Migrations should never use `force`.

`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3` **edits an already-shipped migration** to add `force: true`. That's out of scope for this PR and is a data-loss footgun (drops `top_topics` if ever re-run), plus it breaks migration reproducibility.

`db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3` — `add_column … default: 1, null: false` on `posts` rewrites the entire table under an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on older PostgreSQL. On a large forum this is multi-minute downtime with no strategy noted. Consider nullable-add + backfill + constraint.

**9. `lib/topic_retriever.rb:41` — a full feed poll runs synchronously inside a per-request job.** One embed miss triggers `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` — download and import the *entire* feed — inline. Combined with the hourly schedule and no lock, two polls can interleave; the unique index then raises `RecordNotUnique` inside `Topic.transaction`, aborting the job. Fix: a distributed lock around `poll_feed`, and enqueue rather than inline-call.

**10. No timeouts, size limits, or error handling on outbound fetches.** `open(url)` in `topic_embed.rb:48` and `poll_feed.rb:29` have no read/open timeout, no response size cap, and no redirect restriction — a slow or huge remote resource hangs a Sidekiq worker indefinitely. Also `topic_embed.rb` calls `open` without requiring `open-uri` itself (it only works because `poll_feed.rb` requires it globally) — in a lazily-loaded environment `import_remote` degrades to `Kernel#open` and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` and explicit timeouts.

**11. `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17` — substring origin check.** `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` passes for *any origin that is a substring of* `discourseUrl` (e.g. origin `https://forum.example.co` against `discourseUrl = "https://forum.example.com"`). Compare against a parsed origin with `===`. Relatedly, `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` (`embed_controller.rb:28`) is not a valid header value — browsers ignore it, so the page becomes framable by *anyone*, not just `embeddable_host`. Prefer `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <embeddable_host>`.
No spec renders any of the three new templates — which is exactly why issue #1 ships. Add `render_views` to `embed_controller_spec`.

`spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` sets expectations on the subject's own private methods (`topic_retriever.expects(:perform_retrieve)`), so it verifies the mock wiring, not the throttle or host logic. Nothing exercises the Redis path.

`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` never parses a feed. Two of its four tests pass vacuously (`feed_polling_enabled?` defaults false, so stubbing only `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` proves nothing). A fixture-based RSS 2.0 + Atom test would have caught issue #3.
No spec at all for `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`.

`embed_controller_spec.rb:44` still asserts on `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` while the controller now calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, …)`; it only passes because jobs execute inline in test **[verify]**. That implicit coupling should be made explicit (assert the enqueue).
`embed_controller_spec.rb:8` ("is 404 without an embed_url") passes because `embeddable_host` is blank and `ensure_embeddable` raises first — the `params.require` path is never actually exercised.

**16. Dead / incorrect code signalling unfinished work.** `poll_feed.rb:20` defines `feed_key` (a `feed-modified:` cache key) that is never called — the conditional-GET / Last-Modified optimization it implies was never wired up, so every hourly poll re-downloads and re-hashes the whole feed. `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` requires `email/sender`, which the job does not use.

**17. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:36` passes `bypass_rate_limiter: true` to `PostRevisor#revise!` [verify]** — no handling for that option appears in the diff's `post_revisor.rb` hunks. If it isn't supported upstream, the option is silently ignored and hourly feed updates can trip edit rate limits.
`app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — `contents << "…"` mutates the caller's string argument; raises `FrozenError` under frozen string literals. Use `contents + "…"`.
`topic_embed.rb` — a re-import never updates the topic title, so upstream title corrections are ignored; `embed.update_column` also skips `updated_at`.

`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9` — unconditional 30s reload with no attempt cap: if retrieval can never succeed, every open tab polls the server forever. Combined with `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` on that response, a cached loading page can also delay the first successful render.

`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8` — `window.onload =` clobbers any other handler (use `addEventListener`); `if (parent)` is always truthy (`parent === window` when unframed); height is measured exactly once, so late-loading images leave the iframe mis-sized.

`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5` — no null check on `#discourse-comments`, and `discourseUrl + "embed/best…"` silently breaks unless the host page includes a trailing slash. Neither the required globals nor the required div are documented anywhere.

Referer-based access control is trivially spoofable by non-browser clients and *fails legitimately* when browsers omit the header (e.g. an HTTPS parent page framing an HTTP forum) — worth a comment acknowledging it's a convenience check, not a security boundary.
`config/locales/server.en.yml:38` — `embed.permalink` is added but never referenced.

`db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` — whitespace-only churn that *removes* the trailing newline; `lib/post_revisor.rb:14` removes a blank line for no reason. Several new files also lack trailing newlines. Unrelated noise in the diff.
`topic_embed.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` should be `require`; `require_dependency` is for autoloadable app code.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **2. Stored XSS — `raw_html` posts are never sanitized.** (`app/models/post.rb:131`, `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`, `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13`, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19`)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a `cook_method` of `:raw_html` and makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly when that mode is set (`app/models/post.rb`), bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, using HTML content sourced from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content`) or fetched remote pages (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses Readability output). None of these paths sanitize or strip dangerous attributes/protocols; `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href/src`. Finally, the embed view renders `post.cooked` using `raw` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so any injected HTML/JS stored in `raw` will execute. This is a verifiable stored XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `poll_feed` does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content...)` with **no tag/attribute whitelist**. The unescape actively converts a feed's escaped `<script>` into a live `<script>`. The result is stored as `cooked` and emitted via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed view *and* returned as `cooked` in topic JSON, where Ember inserts it as-is on the main forum. Feeds routinely carry third-party/user-contributed HTML.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code takes `i.content`, calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization/whitelist. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. The `Post#cook` change explicitly bypasses the cooking/sanitization pipeline for `:raw_html` (`return raw`), so the HTML is effectively trusted verbatim. The new embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and the accompanying spec asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, confirming the unsanitized HTML is what gets rendered. Therefore a feed that contains escaped tags like `<script>...` would be unescaped into active `<script>` and stored/rendered, creating an XSS vector introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicEmbed.import` line 13 interpolates the URL into an attribute without escaping: `"#{url}"`. In the feed path `url` comes straight from `i.link`/`i.id`, and the only guard is a `^https?://` prefix match — so `http://x/'+onmouseover='alert(1)` passes validation and breaks out of the attribute. `I18n.t` does not escape interpolations.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `"...#{url}..."` directly into `contents`. In the feed path (`Jobs::PollFeed`), `url` comes from `i.link`/`i.id` and the only check is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other HTML-breaking characters. Because the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged (bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore a URL like `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)` would break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML, making this a real XSS vector introduced by the diff. `I18n.t` interpolation does not auto-escape in this context since the resulting string is treated as raw HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `import_remote`'s Readability whitelist keeps `href` with **any value**, so `<a href="javascript:...">` survives.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, remote HTML is parsed via `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: ..., attributes: %w[href src])` and then persisted via `TopicEmbed.import(..., doc.content)`. The created post is explicitly marked `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `raw_html`, bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. There is no additional sanitization/URI-scheme validation in this diff for `href`/`src` values, so if Readability preserves an `<a href="javascript:...">` attribute value (as the finding claims), that dangerous link will be stored and rendered verbatim. The diff therefore introduces a credible XSS/vector via untrusted remote content when raw HTML rendering is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **3. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — `i.content.scrub` crashes on RSS 2.0 feeds, killing the whole poll.**
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying bug: calling `i.content.scrub` can crash when RSS items lack a populated `content` field (common in RSS 2.0), leading to a nil-related exception and breaking the poll. The candidate doesn’t mention the specific fallback to `description`, but it identifies the same failure mode/source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **4. `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-15` — unauthenticated, unvalidated, unthrottled job enqueue.** `embed_url` is taken straight from the query string with no format or host validation and handed to `Jobs.enqueue`. Validation only happens *inside* the job, so anyone can enqueue unbounded Sidekiq work by varying the URL (the Redis throttle also runs inside the job and is keyed per-URL, so it doesn't help). Fix: validate scheme + host against `embeddable_host` in the controller before enqueueing, and apply a per-IP `RateLimiter`.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` is taken directly from the query string and, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found, is passed straight into `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` with no validation of scheme/format/host at the controller layer. The only controller-side guard (`ensure_embeddable`) validates `request.referer`’s host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, not the `embed_url` parameter itself, so it does not prevent enqueueing jobs with arbitrary `embed_url` values. The job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) only checks presence, and host validation/throttling happens inside `TopicRetriever`, with throttling keyed by the full URL, so varying `embed_url` can bypass the throttle and still enqueue unbounded work. This is a verifiable unthrottled enqueue/DoS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **5. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:15` / migration — no URL normalization.** Lookup and the unique index are exact string matches, so `?utm_source=…`, trailing slash, `http` vs `https`, and `#fragment` variants each create a *separate topic for the same article* — squarely against the stated "URL handling" intent. Also, `t.string :embed_url` is `varchar(255)` by default; a longer URL raises `StatementInvalid` inside the job. Fix: normalize (strip fragment, canonicalize scheme/host case, optionally strip tracking params) before lookup/insert and widen the column.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `TopicEmbed.import` and `topic_id_for_embed` key off `embed_url` via exact string match (`where(embed_url: url)`), and the migration enforces uniqueness on that raw string (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). No normalization is performed (scheme, trailing slash, fragments, query params), so different textual variants of the same page will create separate `topic_embeds` (and thus separate topics) instead of reusing/updating one. Additionally, the migration defines `t.string :embed_url` with the default 255-character limit; `TopicEmbed.create!` can raise a DB error for longer URLs, and nothing in the diff bounds/checks `url` length before insert (e.g., `PollFeed` and `import_remote` accept arbitrary URLs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **6. `lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28` — non-atomic throttle can wedge a URL forever.** `SETNX` then a separate `EXPIRE`: if the process dies or Redis fails between the two calls, the key has no TTL and that URL is throttled permanently. Fix: `$redis.set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)`.

adjudication.rationale:
In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` the throttle uses two separate Redis calls:

```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
```

Because `SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are not atomic, if the process crashes or loses Redis connectivity after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key can be left without a TTL. That would cause `retrieved_recently?` to keep returning `true` for that URL indefinitely (until the key is manually deleted), effectively wedging retrieval. Using a single `SET` with `NX` and `EX` (or a Lua script / MULTI) avoids this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **7. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:62-70` — `absolutize_urls` handles only root-relative URLs.**

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are only rewritten when `href`/`src` starts with `'/'` (root-relative). Other valid relative forms (e.g., `"images/foo.png"`, `"../path"`, `"./path"`, protocol-relative `"//cdn..."`) are left unchanged, despite the method comment claiming it converts relative URLs to absolute. This is a concrete correctness gap in the diff that can break imported RSS/HTML rendering when relative URLs aren’t root-relative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Protocol-relative `//cdn.example.com/x.png` starts with `/`, so `sub(/^\/+/,'')` mangles it into `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png` — a working URL is turned into a broken one.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both links and images are rewritten when the attribute `start_with?('/')`. That condition matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`. The rewrite does `href.sub(/^\/+/,'')`, turning `//cdn.example.com/x.png` into `cdn.example.com/x.png`, and then prefixes it with the embed page’s host (`prefix`), producing `http://<embed_host>/cdn.example.com/x.png`, which is a different (broken) URL. Same issue exists for `img src`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Document-relative URLs (`images/x.png`, `../x.png`) are not rewritten at all and stay broken.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites `` and `` values that `start_with?('/')`. It does not handle document-relative paths like `images/x.png`, `./x.png`, or `../x.png` (nor other relative forms), so those URLs remain unchanged and may be broken when the content is embedded/imported. See `app/models/topic_embed.rb` where the rewrite condition is `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')` only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `<base href>` in the source document is ignored.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces URL “absolutization” in `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, but it only rewrites `href`/`src` values that start with `/` (root-relative). It does not parse or respect an HTML `<base href="...">` element from the source document (and also won’t fix other relative forms like `images/a.png` or `../a`). When importing via `import_remote` (`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read)`), any extracted content containing relative links that depend on `<base href>` will remain incorrect because the base URL is ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` uses `force: true`, which silently `DROP`s an existing `topic_embeds` table. Migrations should never use `force`.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. Even though migrations normally run once, this option can cause silent data loss in cases where the table already exists (e.g., a partially applied migration, manual table creation, or rerunning in certain workflows). This is a real risk introduced by the diff and `force: true` is unnecessary for a new table migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3` **edits an already-shipped migration** to add `force: true`. That's out of scope for this PR and is a data-loss footgun (drops `top_topics` if ever re-run), plus it breaks migration reproducibility.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. Editing an already-existing migration is generally a correctness/reproducibility problem (migrations are expected to be immutable once shipped), and `force: true` makes Rails drop the table if it already exists when the migration is run, which is a real data-loss footgun if the migration is ever re-run in an environment where `top_topics` exists (e.g., partial restores, manual runs, or schema drift).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3` — `add_column … default: 1, null: false` on `posts` rewrites the entire table under an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on older PostgreSQL. On a large forum this is multi-minute downtime with no strategy noted. Consider nullable-add + backfill + constraint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions common at the time of this code (and in general “older PostgreSQL”), adding a column with a non-NULL default can trigger a full table rewrite and requires an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on the `posts` table. Since `posts` is typically very large on a forum, this can cause significant downtime. The migration includes no phased approach (nullable add + backfill + constraint) to avoid that lock, so the operational risk is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. That means a single embed miss (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` enqueued from `EmbedController#best`) can synchronously download/parse the whole feed and import every item before falling back to `fetch_http`, making the retrieve job potentially very slow and redundant with the scheduled hourly poll.

Also, there is no locking/coordination: `PollFeed` has no distributed lock and `TopicEmbed.import` does a check-then-create (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` outside the transaction) followed by `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. Two concurrent polls (scheduled + on-demand, or two on-demand) can race on the same `embed_url` and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which is not rescued and would abort the job/transaction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **10. No timeouts, size limits, or error handling on outbound fetches.** `open(url)` in `topic_embed.rb:48` and `poll_feed.rb:29` have no read/open timeout, no response size cap, and no redirect restriction — a slow or huge remote resource hangs a Sidekiq worker indefinitely. Also `topic_embed.rb` calls `open` without requiring `open-uri` itself (it only works because `poll_feed.rb` requires it globally) — in a lazily-loaded environment `import_remote` degrades to `Kernel#open` and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` and explicit timeouts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple outbound fetches using `open(...)` with no explicit `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`, size cap, or error handling: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). That is a verifiable robustness/security risk (workers can be tied up on slow/large responses; open-uri will also follow redirects by default). Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url)` but `topic_embed.rb` does not `require 'open-uri'` (only `poll_feed.rb` does). Since `import_remote` is invoked from other code paths in the diff (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and the Disqus Thor task), in a lazy-loaded environment it may hit `Kernel#open` without open-uri being loaded and fail (e.g., `Errno::ENOENT` trying to open a local file named like the URL).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **11. `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17` — substring origin check.** `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` passes for *any origin that is a substring of* `discourseUrl` (e.g. origin `https://forum.example.co` against `discourseUrl = "https://forum.example.com"`). Compare against a parsed origin with `===`. Relatedly, `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` (`embed_controller.rb:28`) is not a valid header value — browsers ignore it, so the page becomes framable by *anyone*, not just `embeddable_host`. Prefer `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <embeddable_host>`.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same underlying vulnerability: using `indexOf`/substring matching for origin validation is unsafe because a malicious origin/domain that appears as a substring of the trusted URL can bypass the check (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`-style). The candidate also adds extra related framing-header concerns, but it clearly identifies the same core issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec renders any of the three new templates — which is exactly why issue #1 ships. Add `render_views` to `embed_controller_spec`.

`spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` sets expectations on the subject's own private methods (`topic_retriever.expects(:perform_retrieve)`), so it verifies the mock wiring, not the throttle or host logic. Nothing exercises the Redis path.

adjudication.rationale: The spec in `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` does set expectations on `perform_retrieve` (a private implementation detail) and stubs `retrieved_recently?`, so it does not exercise the real Redis-based throttling path in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`. However, this is a test-quality/design critique rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff; the production logic can still be correct even if the test doesn’t cover the Redis path. Also, the spec *does* indirectly exercise host validation by asserting `perform_retrieve` is not called when the host is invalid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` never parses a feed. Two of its four tests pass vacuously (`feed_polling_enabled?` defaults false, so stubbing only `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` proves nothing). A fixture-based RSS 2.0 + Atom test would have caught issue #3.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` is only invoked when all three conditions are true: `feed_polling_enabled?`, `feed_polling_url.present?`, and `embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" stub only `feed_polling_url` or `embed_by_username` to `nil` but do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`. Given the newly introduced site setting default `feed_polling_enabled: false` in `config/site_settings.yml`, these tests will pass even if `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` checks were broken, because the first condition prevents `poll_feed` from being called. Also, no spec exercises `poll_feed`'s actual behavior (parsing via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`), so the suite does not verify feed parsing/importing at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec at all for `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` and does not add a corresponding spec file for it (there are new specs for `Jobs::PollFeed`, `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, and `TopicEmbed`, but none for `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`). However, “no spec” is not itself a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code; it’s a testing coverage/process concern rather than a concrete defect in behavior shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed_controller_spec.rb:44` still asserts on `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` while the controller now calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, …)`; it only passes because jobs execute inline in test **[verify]**. That implicit coupling should be made explicit (assert the enqueue).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` enqueues a job when no topic is found: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and does not call `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` still expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` in the “no previous embed” case. That expectation no longer matches the controller’s behavior and is therefore a real defect in the test (it will fail unless the test environment happens to run enqueued jobs inline, which is an implicit coupling).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed_controller_spec.rb:8` ("is 404 without an embed_url") passes because `embeddable_host` is blank and `ensure_embeddable` raises first — the `params.require` path is never actually exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best` and immediately raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. In the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do get :best ... end`, nothing stubs `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, whose default in `config/site_settings.yml` is `''` (blank). Therefore the request fails due to `ensure_embeddable` (“embeddable host not set”) before the action body executes, so `params.require(:embed_url)` is not reached for the missing-parameter case. The example passes but does not actually verify behavior when `embed_url` is absent under a valid embeddable configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **16. Dead / incorrect code signalling unfinished work.** `poll_feed.rb:20` defines `feed_key` (a `feed-modified:` cache key) that is never called — the conditional-GET / Last-Modified optimization it implies was never wired up, so every hourly poll re-downloads and re-hashes the whole feed. `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` requires `email/sender`, which the job does not use.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `def feed_key` is introduced but there are no calls to `feed_key` anywhere in that file/class (and nothing in the diff wires it into `poll_feed`), so it is dead code and any implied caching/conditional-fetch logic is not implemented. Separately, `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` adds `require_dependency 'email/sender'` but the job never references `Email::Sender` (or anything from that file) in `execute`, making it an unused dependency load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **17. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:36` passes `bypass_rate_limiter: true` to `PostRevisor#revise!` [verify]** — no handling for that option appears in the diff's `post_revisor.rb` hunks. If it isn't supported upstream, the option is silently ignored and hourly feed updates can trip edit rate limits.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` calling `PostRevisor#revise!` with `bypass_rate_limiter: true`, and the shown hunk in `post_revisor.rb` does not add logic for that option. However, the diff does not show the full `PostRevisor` implementation—handling for `@opts[:bypass_rate_limiter]` could already exist elsewhere in the file (outside the displayed hunks) or in related code. Therefore the claim that the option is unsupported/ignored (and will cause rate-limit issues) is not verifiable from this diff alone and is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — `contents << "…"` mutates the caller's string argument; raises `FrozenError` under frozen string literals. Use `contents + "…"`.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents << "..."` does mutate the passed-in String, but the diff provides no indication that callers pass a frozen string (no `frozen_string_literal: true` pragma, and typical sources like `Readability::Document#content` / `CGI.unescapeHTML` return mutable strings). Appending the “imported from” footer also appears intentional for constructing the post body. The claim that this will raise `FrozenError` is therefore speculative/not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `topic_embed.rb` — a re-import never updates the topic title, so upstream title corrections are ignored; `embed.update_column` also skips `updated_at`.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found (`embed` present), the code only updates the associated post content (via `PostRevisor#revise!`) and then updates `embed.content_sha1`. The passed-in `title` argument is ignored on re-import, so upstream title changes will never be reflected in the Discourse topic/post title. Additionally, it uses `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`, and `update_column` bypasses callbacks/timestamps, so `topic_embeds.updated_at` will not change on re-import updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9` — unconditional 30s reload with no attempt cap: if retrieval can never succeed, every open tab polls the server forever. Combined with `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` on that response, a cached loading page can also delay the first successful render.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb a setTimeout unconditionally calls document.location.reload() every 30000ms, with no max-attempt/backoff/stop condition. If the background retrieval (Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)) never results in a TopicEmbed (e.g., misconfiguration, invalid URL, repeated failure), any client stuck on the loading view will continue reloading indefinitely, generating repeated requests. Additionally, EmbedController#best calls discourse_expires_in 1.minute for all responses (including the loading render), so if intermediate/proxy caching honors that, reloads within that minute can keep serving the cached loading page even after the embed becomes available, delaying the first successful render.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8` — `window.onload =` clobbers any other handler (use `addEventListener`); `if (parent)` is always truthy (`parent === window` when unframed); height is measured exactly once, so late-loading images leave the iframe mis-sized.

`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5` — no null check on `#discourse-comments`, and `discourseUrl + "embed/best…"` silently breaks unless the host page includes a trailing slash. Neither the required globals nor the required div are documented anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` which unconditionally does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the host page doesn’t include an element with id `discourse-comments`, this will throw at runtime (`Cannot read properties of null`). Also, `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` assumes `discourseUrl` ends with `/`; if it does not, the constructed URL becomes invalid (e.g., `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`). The claim about “not documented anywhere” isn’t directly verifiable from this diff, but the two runtime failure modes are present in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-based access control is trivially spoofable by non-browser clients and *fails legitimately* when browsers omit the header (e.g. an HTTPS parent page framing an HTTP forum) — worth a comment acknowledging it's a convenience check, not a security boundary.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` enforces access solely by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and then sets `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"`. This is (1) not a strong security boundary because non-browser clients can supply an arbitrary `Referer` header, and (2) brittle because legitimate requests will be rejected when the browser omits/suppresses the Referer (e.g., referrer-policy stripping on HTTPS→HTTP downgrade, privacy settings, or explicit `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`). The behavior is directly implied by the diff (it raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `request.referer` is blank/invalid).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `config/locales/server.en.yml:38` — `embed.permalink` is added but never referenced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and within the shown changes there is no code/view that references `t('embed.permalink')` (the embed views use `embed.title`, `embed.start_discussion`, `embed.continue`, `embed.loading`, `embed.imported_from`). However, an unused i18n key is not a verifiable functional defect from this diff alone—it's at most dead/extra localization content and could be intended for future use or referenced elsewhere outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` — whitespace-only churn that *removes* the trailing newline; `lib/post_revisor.rb:14` removes a blank line for no reason. Several new files also lack trailing newlines. Unrelated noise in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show whitespace-only churn: `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` changes only trailing spaces and ends with `\ No newline at end of file`, and several newly added files also lack a trailing newline. `lib/post_revisor.rb` also removes an empty line. However, these are formatting/style/noise issues, not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `topic_embed.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` should be `require`; `require_dependency` is for autoloadable app code.

adjudication.rationale: In topic_embed.rb the line `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` is unusual because `require_dependency` is primarily meant to make Rails track application files for reloading, but it still ultimately loads the target via Ruby require/load and will successfully load a gem like Nokogiri. The diff does not show any malfunction, correctness bug, or security issue caused by this; at most it’s an unnecessary/idiomatic concern (a style nit), not a verifiable defect introduced by the change.
